critical_code_review_comments: compute_permission_warnings (admin_permission_service.py:427-434) `implied` map is missing labels.package.approve->labels.package.request.view and labels.blacklist.approve->labels.blacklist.request.view (present in has_permission but not here). Effect: an approver_no_queue warning could be triggered for package/blacklist approvers even when the approve grant implicitly gives the view. Minor UX warning-noise issue only; production has_permission is correct.

sensitive_requests.py::_apply_package re-reads only package_revision but not the full label payload again — change_label_package internally re-validates, so this is fine, but if the label were deleted between request and approval the approval would 500. Consider a soft 404 wrapper.

admin_permission_service.py:316 legacy_role_for_permission maps ANY `labels.*` prefix (including labels.blacklist/labels.package) to admin_support. Currently harmless because permission_for_request routes blacklist/package to specific perms handled by assert_admin_permission, but future refactors relying on legacy_role_for_permission could misroute — worth a comment or a labels.package/blacklist -> admin_finance/super_admin branch.

Blacklist approval writes account_status='active' unconditionally on unblacklist, ignoring prior states like 'suspended'. Minor lifecycle regression risk (unblacklist could inadvertently re-activate a suspended label). Consider preserving prior status.
